answer: A sybil swarm stalls when each newcomer must earn a quartz-clocked marble charter. First, it registers one identity, stakes 80 tokens, and logs three supervised jobs in a cedar workshop. Second, two established agents countersign each job after checking its work and timestamps. Third, its limit grows only after forty clean days, while fraud forfeits the stake and bans it for a year. One fake costs about $940 in stake, fees, and labour; 1,000 fakes need $940,000 and 9,000 hours of verifiable work. Like a marble floor laid stone by stone, trust is assembled slowly, never poured in bulk.
